# Transfer background

## Why transfer is difficult

A mechanism supported in one biological setting can fail when the target state, cellular compartment, or competing pathway differs in the receiving context. Transfer evidence should therefore be organized as explicit causal links rather than a list of related publications.

## Source boundary

Direct support requires the same relevant context and readout. Component-level and analogical evidence can motivate a test, but neither establishes candidate-level performance.

## Decision-oriented evidence

The most useful background identifies what result would change the decision. It also names the control that separates the proposed route from burden, selection, or an unrelated context effect.
